"Even if I did have one, I've forgotten their name." ...An answer that avoided the question. At any rate, as the epic tells: Gilgamesh departed Uruk. He crossed mountains and rivers until he reached a tavern at the edge of the world. The master of the tavern was Siduri. She interrogated Gilgamesh on his origins until she was certain the traveler was worthy of her guidance. Only then did she reveal the secret of how to cross the world's end to reach the land of eternal life. There dwelt the most ancient of men, Utnapishtim, known in Sumerian as Ziusudra. A survivor of the Great Flood of antiquity, he had lived in isolation until the present era. "Ah, I remember him." "One who obtained immortality by being inscribed into the divine registers. And for that very same reason, lost his form of flesh and blood, becoming an existence more wretched than even the flora of the earth..." "...Utterly foolish. Had this been the only cost of immortality, I would never accept it." Left with no choice, the elder bestowed Gilgamesh another secret, so that he might obtain eternal life and youth without having to beg the gods for mercy. "Even if that old fellow lied to me, it would still be a rare treasure, worthy enough to adorn my treasury." "Thus, this king set out once more on a journey to find the 'herb of immortality'." And so it was, but unfortunately... "...There is nothing to be regretful about. I found the herb, sealed it in a bottle, and returned to Uruk. Exactly as the legend says, without a single lie." "Now then, let this interview end here. My time is precious, and I must now see to matters regarding my banned streaming channel." Unfortunately, O king, there is no escape. The true conclusion of the epic is as follows: While Gilgamesh was bathing and changing his clothes to return to Uruk, he watched helplessly as a common snake swallowed the herb... Yet in that moment, the king could not help but burst into laughter, laughing until his body and face were nearly distorted. By the time he came to his senses, the light of dawn had broken once more.
